role.q: Tell me about an analysis that changed a business decision.
role.why: Analysts are hired for impact, not for charts.
role.model: Marketing wanted to increase the budget of a campaign that looked profitable. I joined campaign data with returns and found that 30% of its orders were returned, against 12% on average. Net of returns it lost money. We reallocated half the budget to two other channels, which improved the marketing return by about 15% the following quarter.

role.q: Sales dropped 10% last week. How do you investigate?
role.why: Classic case question: structure and curiosity.
role.model: First check the data itself: tracking, pipeline delays, definition changes. Then compare with the same week last year and recent weeks to see if it is unusual. Break it down: by channel, region, product, new vs returning customers, traffic vs conversion vs basket size. Look for internal changes (prices, site releases, stock) and external ones (holidays, weather, competitors). Then share the most likely causes with evidence and next steps.

role.q: How do you define a good KPI?
role.model: It is tied to a goal, clearly defined (numerator, denominator, period, filters), owned by someone, comparable over time and actionable: people know what to do when it moves. I pair it with guardrail metrics so it cannot be improved at the expense of something else.

role.q: How do you make a dashboard people actually use?
role.why: Many dashboards are built and never opened.
role.model: Start from the decisions and questions of its users, not from the available data. Put 3–5 key figures at the top with comparisons, then breakdowns, then details. Consistent definitions, clear titles that state the insight, fast loading. I then check usage statistics and ask users after two weeks what they still do outside the dashboard.

role.q: How would you analyse the result of an A/B test?
role.why: Common for product and marketing analysts.
role.model: Check the test ran as planned: random split, sample ratio, duration, no peeking. Compare the primary metric with a significance test and a confidence interval for the effect, then check guardrail metrics and key segments. Recommend based on the size of the effect and its cost, not just the p-value.

role.q: You find that two dashboards show different revenue for the same month. What do you do?
role.model: Compare the definitions and filters (tax, returns, currency, date used: order or payment), then the sources and refresh times. Reconcile on a small sample of orders to find where they diverge. Fix or document the official definition, align both dashboards, and communicate the change to users.

role.q: Which SQL or Excel functions do you use most and why?
role.model: In SQL: joins, GROUP BY with CASE WHEN for conditional counts, CTEs to keep queries readable, and window functions for rankings and period-over-period changes. In Excel: XLOOKUP, SUMIFS and pivot tables for fast exploration and checks.

role.q: How do you present a result that your audience will not like?
role.model: Lead with the facts and how they were obtained, so the discussion is about the data, not about me. Show the impact, the uncertainty, and what can be done. I share it first with the owner in private when possible, and always come with options or next steps rather than only bad news.
